title: An invented seal and an accursed God
source_text: Ἑξῆς δὲ τοῖς περὶ τοῦ διαγράμματος μηδὲ παρακούσας τῶν περὶ τῆς καλουμένης παρὰ τοῖς ἐκκλησιαστικοῖς σφραγῖδος ἑαυτῷ τινα ἐκτίθεται ἀλλόκοτα καὶ ἀμοιβαίας φωνὰς, ὡς τοῦ μὲν τὴν σφραγῖδα περιτιθέντος καλουμένου πατρὸς, τοῦ δὲ σφραγιζομένου λεγομένου νέου καὶ υἱοῦ καὶ ἀποκρινομένου· κέχρισμαι χρίσματι λευκῷ ἐκ ξύλου ζωῆς, ὅπερ οὐδ᾿ ἐν τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν αἱρέσεων ἠκούσαμεν γίνεσθαι. εἶτα καὶ ἀριθμὸν ὁρίζει λεγόμενον ὑπὸ τῶν παραδιδόντων τὴν σφραγῖδα ἀγγέλων ἑπτὰ, ἑκατέρωθεν τῇ ψυχῇ τοῦ ἀπαλλαττομένου σώματος ἐφισταμένων, τῶν μὲν τοῦ φωτὸς ἑτέρων δὲ τῶν ὀνομαζομένων ἁρχοντικῶν, καὶ λέγει τὸν ἄρχοντα τῶν ὀνομαζομένων ἀρχοντικῶν λέγεσθαι θεὸν κατηραμένον. εἶτ᾿ ἐπιλαβόμενος τῆς λέξεως εὐλόγως κατηγορεῖ τῶν τοῦτο τολμώντων λέγειν· τούτου δ᾿ ἕνεκα καὶ ἡμεῖς συναγανακτοῦμεν τοῖς μεμφομένοις τοὺς τοιούτους. εἰ δή τινες εἰσὶ λέγοντες θεὸν κατηραμένον τὸν Ἰουδαίων, τὸν ὕοντα καὶ βροντῶντα καὶ τοῦδε τοῦ κόσμου δημιουργὸν καὶ Μωϋσέως καὶ τῆς κατ᾿ αὐτὸν κοσμοποιΐας θεόν. ἀλλ᾿ ἔοικε βεβουλῆσθαί τι διὰ τούτων ὁ Κέλσος οὐκ εὔγνωμον ἀλλ᾿ ἀπὸ τοῦ καθ᾿ ἡμῶν ἀφιλοσόφου μίσους πάνυ ἀγνωμονέστατον. ἐβουλήθη γὰρ τοὺς ἀπείρους τῶν ἡμετέρων ἐντυχόντας αὐτοῦ τῇ γραφῇ πολεμῶσαι πρὸς ἡμᾶς, ὡς θεὸν κατηραμένον λέγοντας τὸν τοῦδε τοῦ κόσμου καλὸν δημιουργόν. καὶ δοκεῖ μοι παραπλήσιον Ἰουδαίοις πεποιηκέναι, τοῖς κατὰ τὴν ἀρχὴν (τῆς) τοῦ χριστιανισμοῦ διδασκαλίας κατασκεδάσασι δυσφημίαν τοῦ λόγου, ὡς ἄρα καταθύσαντες παιδίον μεταλαμβάνουσιν αὐτοῦ τῶν σαρκῶν, καὶ πάλιν ὅτι οἱ ἀπὸ τοῦ λόγου τὰ τοῦ σκότου πράττειν βουλόμενοι σβεννύουσι μὲν τὸ φῶς. ἕκαστος δὲ τῇ παρατυχούσῃ μίγνυται· ἥτις δυσφημία παραλόγως πάλαι μὲν πλείστων ὅσων ἐκράτει πείθουσα τοὺς ἀλλοτρίους τοῦ λόγου ὅτι τοιοῦτοί εἰσι Χριστιανοὶ, καὶ νῦν δὲ ἔτι ἀπατᾷ τινας ἀποτρεπομένους διὰ τὰ τοιαῦτα κἂν εἰς κοινωνίαν ἁπλουστέραν λόγων ἥκειν πρὸς Χριστιανούς.
pass_a_gloss: Next after the things about the diagram, not even having misheard (παρακούω) any of the things about what is called among the churchmen (ἐκκλησιαστικοί) the seal (σφραγίς), he sets out for himself some strange things (ἀλλόκοτα) and responsive (ἀμοιβαῖος) utterances (φωνή): that the one putting on (περιτίθημι) the seal is called father, and the one sealed (σφραγίζω) is called young (νέος) and son and answers: 'I have been anointed (χρίω) with white ointment (χρῖσμα) from the tree (ξύλον) of life', which we have not heard is done even among those from the sects (αἵρεσις). Then he also defines (ὁρίζω) a number said by those handing down (παραδίδωμι) the seal, of angels seven, standing by (ἐφίσταμαι) on either side the soul of one departing (ἀπαλλάσσω) the body, some of light, others of those named archontic (ἀρχοντικοί), and he says the ruler (ἄρχων) of those named archontic is called accursed (καταράομαι, perf. pass.) god. Then laying hold (ἐπιλαμβάνομαι) of the phrase (λέξις) he reasonably (εὐλόγως) accuses those daring (τολμάω) to say this; and on account of this we too are indignant together (συναγανακτέω) with those blaming (μέμφομαι) such, if indeed some are saying the God of the Jews is accursed, the one raining (ὕω) and thundering (βροντάω) and creator (δημιουργός) of this world and God of Moses and of the world-making (κοσμοποιΐα) according to him. But Celsus seems to have wished something through these not fair-minded (εὐγνώμων) but from the unphilosophical (ἀφιλόσοφος) hatred (μῖσος) against us most unfair (ἀγνωμονέστατος). For he wished to make hostile (πολεμόω) toward us those inexperienced (ἄπειρος) in our things who read his writing, as if saying the good creator of this world is an accursed god. And he seems to me to have done similarly to Jews, who at the beginning of the teaching of Christianity (χριστιανισμός) scattered (κατασκεδάννυμι) slander (δυσφημία) of the word (λόγος), that having sacrificed (καταθύω) a child (παιδίον) they partake (μεταλαμβάνω) of its flesh, and again that those from the word wishing to do the things of darkness (σκότος) quench (σβέννυμι) the light, and each has intercourse (μίγνυμι) with the woman who happens by (παρατυγχάνω); which slander unreasonably (παραλόγως) of old prevailed over (κρατέω) very many, persuading those foreign (ἀλλότριος) to the word that Christians are such, and now still deceives (ἀπατάω) some, turned away (ἀποτρέπω) through such things from coming even into simpler fellowship (κοινωνία) of words with Christians.
pass_b_english: Next, after what he says about the diagram, Celsus, without having even half-heard what members of the Church call the seal, sets out on his own some strange things and an exchange of words: that the one who puts on the seal is called father, and the one who is sealed is called young one and son, and answers, “I have been anointed with white ointment from the tree of life” (compare Genesis 2:9). We have not heard that this is done even among the sects.

Then he even fixes a number, said to be given by those who hand down the seal: seven angels, who stand on either side by the soul as it departs from the body, some of them angels of light, the others of those called “of the rulers”. And he says that the ruler of those called “of the rulers” is called an accursed god.

Then, seizing on the phrase, he rightly accuses those who dare to say this; and for this reason we too share the indignation of those who blame such people, if indeed there are any who call the God of the Jews accursed, the God who sends rain and thunder, the Creator of this world, the God of Moses and of the account of the world’s making that Moses gave.

But Celsus seems to have intended by this something not fair-minded, but, out of his unphilosophical hatred of us, utterly unfair. For he wanted to set against us those unacquainted with our teaching who read his work, as though we called the good Creator of this world an accursed god. And he seems to me to have done much the same as the Jews, who, when the teaching of Christianity first began, spread slander about the word: that Christians sacrifice a little child and partake of its flesh; and again, that those who follow the word, wishing to do the works of darkness, put out the light, and each lies with whatever woman happens to be beside him. This slander, against all reason, once held sway over very great numbers, persuading those who were strangers to the word that Christians are such people; and even now it still deceives some, who because of such stories turn away from coming even into the simplest conversation with Christians.

choices.choice: The exchange ‘I have been anointed with white ointment from the tree of life’ is Celsus’s report of the alleged rite; put in quotation marks as words he sets out. The ‘tree of life’ is a clear echo of Genesis 2:9 (also Revelation 2:7; 22:2) but sits inside Celsus’s alleged formula, so the citation is placed after the closing quotation mark, outside his words, marked ‘compare’. ‘Seal’ (σφραγίς) is the church’s name for baptism; Origen says Celsus had not even a garbled report of it (μηδὲ παρακούσας). ‘Those called “of the rulers”’ renders τῶν ὀνομαζομένων ἀρχοντικῶν, avoiding the loan word ‘archontic’. ‘Works of darkness’ (τὰ τοῦ σκότου) may echo Romans 13:12 or Ephesians 5:11, but the wording differs; left uncited. ‘The word’ (ὁ λόγος) here means the Christian teaching and is lowercased. ‘Sends rain and thunder’ echoes Celsus’s own phrasing elsewhere in Book 6 for the God of the Jews. The child-eating and lamp-quenching slanders are reported as charges, not affirmed.
agency fixed: πολεμῶσαι means Celsus wanted to set readers against us, not that they 'turn hostile'
μίγνυται rendered plainly 'lies with' instead of the vague 'joins himself with'
παραλόγως is an adverb on ἐκράτει: 'unreasonable as it was' changed to 'against all reason'

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; the English is from the Greek.
